# Measured HANK equilibrium backend comparison

Generated by `tools/reference_validation/benchmark_hank_equilibrium.py` with
three repetitions, alternating method order, and verified single-thread
Accelerate BLAS on the calling thread. The
record binds sources, environment, timings, convergence diagnostics and path
CSV files by SHA-256. Calibration is separate. Cold optimized timings include
creating the workspace and its sparse preconditioner. Warm solves use a 2%
larger shock and the preceding solution; the nearby control starts at steady
state while retaining the preconditioner.

The runner records NumPy/SciPy BLAS identities and OMP/OpenBLAS/MKL/vecLib
environment limits. On macOS 15+ it calls `BLASSetThreading(1)` and checks
`BLASGetThreading()==1` before numerical work, then restores the prior mode.
The environment-only path on other systems is labeled separately and is not
the source of this frozen record.

The reference uses Powell's hybrid method with numerical aggregate Jacobians.
The new method uses analytic household/distribution Jacobian-vector products
and sparse preconditioning. They share the household equations and finite
terminal closure. These are same-grid numerical comparisons, not independent
published stochastic-model replication or a new grid/horizon accuracy study.
The separate `hank_scenario_tree` and `hank_equilibrium` evidence remains valid
for its stated scope; the frozen reference source has not been altered.

Timing observations are specific to the recorded machine and environment.
Tests recompute reported differences and timing summaries and check source
hashes and node accounts. They do not impose a speed threshold. A new
benchmark run must use a new output directory so earlier evidence survives.

Large per-household arrays are not archived here. Their maximum differences
were computed in memory during each recorded solve; reproducing those numbers
requires rerunning the script. Aggregate path differences and node accounts
can be independently recomputed from the retained CSVs. Frozen timing data
documents an observed run and cannot prove timings on another machine.

`prior_uncontrolled/` preserves the initial record, all its CSVs and the exact
runner source used. Those solves converged, but the initial runner's
single-thread guidance was incomplete for Apple Accelerate: setting
OMP/OpenBLAS/MKL variables did not explicitly pin this backend. Its actual
timing observations are retained for provenance and are superseded in the
performance table by the controlled run. The original source is archived
verbatim, including that incomplete guidance.
